Definition: Understandability refers to how easily developers can comprehend and maintain the test code.

Task: Improve the understandability of the test `TestJulianChronology_test_Chronology_date_Temporal.java` (path:- /Users/tenghaha/Projects/New_Agent_understandability_improvement/data/original/threeten-extra/manual/testcases/TestJulianChronology/TestJulianChronology_test_Chronology_date_Temporal.java). The refactored code must be syntactically correct and compilable against the provided CUT signatures. Do not alter the runtime behaviour of the original test: the same methods must be called with the same arguments and produce the same expected outcomes.

The original test contains a large amount of dead code: eight unused `data_*` provider methods and many unused imports. Only `data_samples` feeds the single `@ParameterizedTest`. Removing the noise (without touching what actually runs) is the biggest understandability win. Let me write the cleaned-up version.Compilation succeeded (`COMPILE_OK`). I improved understandability by removing eight unused `data_*` provider methods and all unused imports, formatting the surviving `data_samples` pairs one-per-line with explanatory comments (leap-year quirks and the growing Julian/ISO day offset), adding Javadoc, and renaming the parameter to `expectedJulian` — while keeping the exact same single parameterized assertion and data.
